content: Actin-binding proteins (also known as ABPs) are proteins that bind to actin.[1] This may mean ability to bind actin monomers, or polymers, or both.
Many actin-binding proteins, including α-actinin, β-spectrin, dystrophin, utrophin and fimbrin, do this through the actin-binding calponin homology domain.
This is a list of actin-binding proteins in alphabetical order.
<info> ERM proteins (ezrin, radixin, moesin, plus merlin)
<info> Ezrin (the E of ERM protein family)
<info> PASK (Proline, Alanine rich Ste20 related Kinase)
<info> Phalloidin (not a protein; a small cyclic peptide)
